prerequisites: Fundamentals of Chemical Processes (2nd semester, 2nd year)
Good foundation in physics, chemistry, mathematics, and thermodynamics

learning_outcomes.text: The student will know and relate the variables involved in the processes of matter and energy transfer in the basic operations of Chemical Engineering.
The student will be able to calculate and design equipment for filtration, sedimentation, and fluidization operations.
The student will apply the basic heat transfer equations to particular cases of chemical processes and will be able to estimate individual and global heat transfer coefficients.
The student will be able to calculate and design heat exchangers, condensers, evaporators, and crystallizers for the chemical industry.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluid flow
Transport of non-Newtonian fluids through pipes
Macroscopic balances in non-Newtonian fluid flow
Introduction to fluid flow through porous beds. Filtration
Fundamentals of fluid flow through porous beds
Theory of centrifugation for immiscible liquid separation
Theory of centrifugal sedimentation for solid-liquid separations
Advantages and disadvantages of fluidized beds
Introduction to basic heat transfer operations
Definition and types of heat exchangers
Number of transfer units in heat exchangers
Heat transfer from condensing vapors: dropwise and film condensation (Nusselt's Theory)
Heat transfer to boiling liquids: saturated liquid boiling and forced convection boiling
Operation of tubular evaporators: capacity, economy, multiple effect operation
Fundamentals of crystallization: crystal purity, equilibrium (solubility and phase diagrams), operation yield, enthalpy balances, supersaturation, nucleation and crystal growth

assessment_methods.method: Group tutorials (TG) - practical exercises and active participation

assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as (0.8 * ((P1 + P2)/2) + 0.20 * TG) if both partial exams are passed, or (0.8 * G + 0.2 * TG) if the global exam is passed. A minimum of 4 out of 10 is required for P1, P2, and G, and a minimum overall grade of 5 out of 10 is needed to pass the course. Both the theoretical-practical and problem-solving parts of the exams must achieve at least 30% of their assigned value. For extraordinary calls, the final grade is (0.8 * G + 0.2 * TG), with a minimum of 4 out of 10 for G and 5 out of 10 overall. Differentiated evaluation consists solely of a global final exam. In case of doubt about authorship or unauthorized means, a student may be asked for an oral defense.
